diagnostic_evidence.quote: For each subset of indices $T \subseteq \set{1, \ldots, \omega}$, define $n_T = N\sum_{t \in T} \frac{1}{p_t}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The vector has indices only from 0 to N-1, but the constructed integer n_T need not lie in that range. For example, for N=30 and T containing the primes 2, 3, and 5, n_T=15+10+6=31. Thus x_{n_T} is not an entry of the declared length-30 signal. Reducing n_T modulo N is plausible, but the proof neither does this nor proves that the resulting residue classes remain distinct.

failure_location.quote:
For every possible value of $n_T$, let $x_{n_T} = (-1)^{\abs{T}}$,
For all other indices $n$, set $x_n = 0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define every n_T modulo N and add the elementary number-theoretic argument that distinct subsets give distinct residues modulo N; then update the Fourier calculation accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed one-dimensional witness is not defined for all N, so the two-dimensional witness and the claimed necessity of one sample from every equivalence class are unsupported as written.
issues.title: The ambiguity signal uses indices outside its declared range
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and preserves the construction and all claimed bounds, requiring only a short modular-distinctness argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: D_1 = N_1/\gcd(k, N_1) \qquad , \qquad  D_2 = N_2/\gcd(l, N_2) \qquad , \qquad D = \lcm(D_1, D_2)

issues.failure_explanation: Dividing k by gcd(k,N_1) guarantees coprimality with D_1=N_1/d_1, not with N_1. For example, N_1=12 and k=8 give d_1=4 and k/d_1=2, which is not invertible modulo 12. Consequently the displayed construction of m_j and n_j is not justified under the stated moduli.

failure_location.quote: Since $d_1 = \gcd(k, N_1)$ and $d_2 = \gcd(l, N_2)$, $k/d_1$ and $l/d_2$ must have multiplicative inverses modulo $N_1$ and $N_2$, respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the inverses modulo D_1 and D_2, respectively, and rewrite the subsequent congruences to show that multiplication by d_1 and d_2 lifts them to congruences modulo N_1 and N_2.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that every subsignal entry contains exactly N_1N_2/D matrix entries fails, and the later two-dimensional ambiguity construction relies on that count.
issues.title: The subsignal partition proof invokes nonexistent modular inverses
issues.why_classification: This is a short local correction to the moduli in an otherwise viable coset argument and does not weaken the result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Require a representative DFT coefficient $\tilde{X}_{k, l}$ for each coefficient class

Two DFT coefficients $\tilde{X}_{k l}$ and $\tilde{X}_{k' l'}$ are equivalent, denoted by $(k, l) \sim (k', l')$, if there exists a nonzero integer $\lambda$ that is relatively prime with $D$ satisfying

issues.failure_explanation: For a divisor λ of D, the frequency (λk,λl) belongs to a lower-order equivalence class, but it need not be the particular representative sampled for that class. The input supplies one arbitrary representative value per class, while Line ln:2to1 directly reads the value at the specific frequency (λk,λl). The zero-equivalence theorem does not identify the numerical values of two equivalent coefficients, so it cannot supply this missing datum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prescribe and prove the existence of a compatible sampling/representative scheme for every requested child frequency, or add an exact procedure that obtains the requested coefficient from the sampled equivalent coefficient, for example through the appropriate cyclotomic Galois action.
issues.overall_effect: The high-level reduction to independent one-dimensional inversions is not executable from its stated input for a general choice of sampled representatives.
issues.title: High-level 2D inversion requests coefficients not supplied by its input
issues.why_classification: The intended reduction can plausibly be retained, but it needs a nontrivial compatibility construction or algebraic coefficient-conversion step rather than a mere notation change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $p \divs N_1$, then $\gcd(pk, N_1) = p\gcd(k, N_1) = N_1/(D_1/p)$.
Since $D_1/p < D_1$, the $(pk, pl)$-subsignal was recovered at a previous iteration of the for loop in Line~\ref{ln:outer}.

issues.failure_explanation: The pseudocode does not require increasing divisor order, although correctness depends on smaller D_1 or D_2 subproblems having already been solved. Moreover, the proof's case p|N_1 is insufficient: p may divide N_1 but not D_1, in which case gcd(pk,N_1)=p gcd(k,N_1) is false. For example, k=0 gives gcd(pk,N_1)=N_1, not pN_1. The correct split must depend on whether p divides D_1; if not, p must divide D_2 and the inner-loop dependency must be used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify increasing order in both divisor loops and replace the proof's case split by p|D_1 versus p∤D_1, using p|D_2 in the second case.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the algorithm may access an unrecovered child subsignal, and its supplied proof does not establish that every required child is available.
issues.title: Memoized 2D inversion has an unspecified order and an invalid dependency case split
issues.why_classification: Both the execution order and proof can be repaired locally without changing the dynamic-programming method or its guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Furthermore, solving Eq.~\eqref{eq:ip_form} directly with ILP can be unstable, as there may exist integer linear combinations of the roots of unity that come arbitrarily close, but do not exactly equal, the given DFT coefficients

issues.failure_explanation: The source itself states that distinct integer combinations of roots of unity can be arbitrarily close. Therefore, for any fixed positive ε and without a bound yielding a separation estimate, an incorrect integer y can pass either tolerance test and be returned as the reconstruction. Exact uniqueness does not imply ε-separated sampled spectra.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use exact algebraic verification, or impose explicit coefficient bounds and prove a separation bound that dictates a safe ε; otherwise the procedure must be presented only as a heuristic that can return false positives.
issues.overall_effect: The lattice implementation has no correctness guarantee for arbitrary integer inputs at positive tolerance and may return a wrong signal rather than merely report failure.
issues.title: Positive-tolerance verification can accept an incorrect integer signal
issues.why_classification: Preserving a guaranteed arbitrary-integer reconstruction requires exact verification or a new quantitative separation theory; merely tuning ε cannot resolve the source's admitted arbitrarily-close alternatives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since the correct ${\bf b}$ lies within $1/\beta_3$ of ${\bf x}^*$, rounding succeeds for sufficiently large $\beta_3$ values.
Any vector in the lattice may be written as ${\tt B}\coeffs$ for a vector ${\bm \alpha} \in \mathbb{Z}^{N}$ and $\gamma \in \mathbb{Z}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Entrywise flooring perturbs each basis entry by less than 1/β_3 after rescaling, but a lattice vector is an integer combination of basis columns. Its perturbation can therefore grow proportionally to the 1-norm of the coefficient vector, here roughly ||α||_1+|γ|, and need not be below 1/β_3. With unbounded integer signals, the fixed choice of β_3 can make the purported solution vector too far from x* for entrywise rounding to recover it.

failure_location.quote: \State ${\tt B}^* \gets$ the LLL reduction of $\lfloor\beta_3{\tt B}\rfloor$ \label{ln:LLL}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive a truncation-error bound that includes the lattice coefficient norm and choose β_3 adaptively from a valid coefficient bound, or replace the truncation by an exact representation of the algebraic basis entries.
issues.overall_effect: Even if LLL identifies the truncated-lattice vector corresponding to the intended coefficients, the reconstruction and rounding step can fail for signal values beyond the unanalysed truncation range.
issues.title: Basis truncation error is not bounded by 1 over the scale
issues.why_classification: A bounded-input version can be repaired with a contained precision analysis and adaptive scaling, but the current fixed-scale justification does not cover the advertised unbounded integer setting.
